title: Sell Mineral Rights in Booth, WV
metaTitle: Sell Mineral Rights in Booth, WV | Monongalia County
metaDescription: Booth, WV mineral owner near the Blacksville coal and gas belt? We buy small fractional Monongalia County interests directly, no obligation to sell.
heroLead: Booth is a small unincorporated community in Monongalia County, close enough to the Blacksville mining complex that its mineral history is bound up in the same layered coal-and-gas ownership as its larger neighbor.
intro: Ownership around Booth tends to trace back to small farm tracts that sat adjacent to, or on top of, coal reserves mined by underground operations over the past century. Gas leasing here often came later, and the mineral estate a family holds today may be a narrow slice of what the original tract contained.

We buy mineral and royalty interests near Booth directly, confirming the specific estate and percentage a family holds before naming a figure, since these tracts are frequently fractional and layered with older reservations.

sections.heading: A narrow gas estate on top of old coal reservations
paragraphs: Many Booth-area tracts have coal already reserved to a mining company from a deed decades old, leaving the current mineral owner with an oil and gas interest only. We confirm that distinction before pricing your interest, since it changes what's actually available to buy.

sections.heading: Small community, scattered heirs
paragraphs: As with much of rural Monongalia County, Booth-area mineral tracts have split among heirs over multiple generations without a formal partition. A single original tract can now have owners spread across several states, each holding a small undivided percentage.

sections.heading: How we confirm your fractional share
paragraphs: We trace the deed and, where needed, probate records back to the original tract to establish exactly what percentage you hold, then check whether the tract is under an active lease or unit before making an offer.

faqs.question: How do I know if my mineral rights near Booth include the coal or just oil and gas?
faqs.answer: It depends on the deed history. If coal was reserved to a mining company in an earlier transaction, your interest may be oil and gas only, which we confirm before making an offer.

faqs.question: My share of the tract is very small. Is it still worth selling?
faqs.answer: Often yes. We routinely buy small fractional shares once we've confirmed the exact percentage from the recorded chain of title.

faqs.question: Is there active gas leasing near Booth right now?
faqs.answer: Leasing activity varies by specific tract. We check current lease and unit status in Monongalia County as part of evaluating your interest.

faqs.question: What paperwork should I gather before contacting you?
faqs.answer: Anything you have, an old deed, a lease, a probate document, helps, but we can locate the recorded chain of title ourselves if you don't have those on hand.
